signals.content: Manage AI agents (Codex) on many computers from one Claude Code session — dispatch, callbacks, notifications, dashboard, Claude Code plugin
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 72. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: cxfydhcg/agent-fleet

Brief: This open‑source tool enables centralized management of multiple AI agents (Codex) across a fleet of computers from a single Claude Code session. It provides dispatching of tasks, callback handling, real‑time notifications, and a dashboard for monitoring. Integration is available as a Claude Code plugin, facilitating streamlined orchestration without requiring extensive custom development. Current documentation is limited; further testing is needed to confirm scalability and security posture.

signals.content: Self-hosted control plane for AI dev configuration. Sync skills across machines, developers and coding agents over MCP.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: dchristopoulos/AIStack
Brief: AIStack is a self‑hosted control plane designed for AI development configuration. It enables synchronization of skills, settings, and code agents across multiple machines and developers via a Managed Control Protocol (MCP). The platform aims to streamline collaborative AI workflows while keeping data and execution within the organization’s own infrastructure. Current documentation indicates functional prototypes, but large‑scale performance and security assessments are still pending.

signals.title: @MizarVision: Middle East | Satellite imagery reveals precision damage to critical Gulf infrastructure New satellite imagery published in a Reuters visual
signals.content: Middle East | Satellite imagery reveals precision damage to critical Gulf infrastructure New satellite imagery published in a Reuters visual investigation documents damage to some of the Gulf’s most strategically important energy and infrastructure facilities following Iranian and Iran-aligned strikes. 🇶🇦 Ras Laffan, Qatar Airbus Pléiades Neo imagery shows severe damage to one of two LNG “cold boxes” hit during the conflict. These systems super-cool natural gas into liquid form and are extremely difficult to replace. QatarEnergy has estimated that full repairs could take years. 🇦🇪 Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant, UAE Satellite imagery shows damage to the roof of a building housing critical electrical equipment. The May 17 strike forced one of the plant’s four reactors onto emergency diesel generators. 🇦🇪 Jebel Ali Port, UAE Planet Labs imagery shows damage to a manifold following a March 1 strike. Operations at the port were temporarily suspended. 🇸🇦 Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia Airbus imagery shows damage to storage/process tanks at Saudi Aramco’s major Abqaiq oil-processing facility following a July 27 attack. Reuters says Iran and allied forces have carried out at least 135 drone and missile strikes against 84 infrastructure sites across Gulf states since the war began on February 28. The imagery highlights how highly specific components — not only large facilities — have repeatedly been hit, causing disruptions far beyond the immediate blast areas. Satellite imagery: Airbus Defence and Space / Planet Labs
